claims.evidence: This is inferred from gene expression and cluster frequency data.

claims.claim: Flow cytometric analysis confirmed both a decrease in BLKposRORγtpos and BLKposRORγtneg γδ T cell populations, as well as a decreased level of BLK expression in neonatal thymus.
claims.source: Similar to our observations in E17 γδ T cells, flow cytometric analysis confirmed both a decrease in BLKposRORγtpos and BLKposRORγtneg γδ T cell populations, as well as a decreased level of BLK expression (Figure 4E, F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 4E and 4F.

claims.claim: There was an increased frequency of immature CD24high73negSLAMF1posSLAMF6pos cluster with characteristics of αβ T cells (c14) in B6.Sh2d1a-/- D9 thymic γδ T cells.
claims.source: In addition, we observed an increased frequency of immature CD24high73negSLAMF1posSLAMF6pos cluster with characteristics of αβ T cells (c14) in B6.Sh2d1a-/- D9 thymic γδ T cells (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: Flow cytometric analysis revealed a significant increase in immature CD24pos73negBLKnegRORγtpos γδ T cells in neonatal thymus.
claims.source: While this increase did not reach the level of significance, presumably due to the very low number of c14 cells in the dataset, flow cytometric analysis revealed a significant increase in immature CD24pos73negBLKnegRORγtpos γδ T cells, a phenotype consistent with γδ T cells that have been diverted to the αβ developmental pathway (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: There was an increased frequency of immature CD24pos73low/pos SLAMF1posSLAMF6pos S1pr1-enriched c4 and c5 clusters in B6.Sh2d1a-/- neonatal thymus.
claims.source: Last, we observed an increased frequency of immature CD24pos73low/pos SLAMF1posSLAMF6pos S1pr1-enriched c4 and c5 clusters, but not the closely related Cd200-enriched c10 cluster (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: There was a decreased frequency of the CD24low73negSLAMF1posF6low γδT17 c6 cluster in B6.Sh2d1a-/- neonatal thymus.
claims.source: Among the mature neonatal γδ T cells, we observed a decreased frequency of the CD24low73negSLAMF1posF6low γδT17 c6 cluster, which was consistent with our previous observation of decreased IL-17 production in B6.Sh2d1a-/- neonatal γδ T cells (Dienz et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison and is consistent with previous observations.

claims.claim: There was a striking loss of the CD24low73highSLAMF1lowF6highF7neg γδT2 c13 cluster in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice.
claims.source: Interestingly, we observed a striking loss of the CD24low73highSLAMF1lowF6highF7neg γδT2 c13 cluster in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice, as well as a decreased frequency of the mature CD24low73highSLAMF1lowF6lowF7high γδT1 c8 cluster (Figure 4A–D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison shown in Figures 4A-D.

claims.claim: There was a decreased frequency of the mature CD24low73highSLAMF1lowF6lowF7high γδT1 c8 cluster in B6.Sh2d1a-/- neonatal thymus.
claims.source: Interestingly, we observed a striking loss of the CD24low73highSLAMF1lowF6highF7neg γδT2 c13 cluster in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice, as well as a decreased frequency of the mature CD24low73highSLAMF1lowF6lowF7high γδT1 c8 cluster (Figure 4A–D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison shown in Figures 4A-D.

claims.claim: These findings were consistent with an SAP-dependent loss of both the IL-4- and IFN-γ-producing γδNKT and non-γδNKT γδT1 cells.
claims.source: These findings were consistent with an SAP-dependent loss of both the IL-4- and IFN-γ-producing γδNKT and non-γδNKT γδT1 cells (discussed further below).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the cluster frequency data.

claims.claim: A comparison of B6 adult thymic γδ T cells between B6 and B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice recapitulated many of the observations of the neonatal thymus.
claims.source: A comparison of B6 adult thymic γδ T cells between B6 and B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice recapitulated many of our observations of the neonatal thymus, although to a somewhat lesser degree.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the adult thymus data.

claims.claim: There was a small but significant decrease in the frequency of the CD24highCD73low adult thymic c1 and c2 clusters in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice.
claims.source: For example, we observed a small but significant decrease in the frequency of the CD24highCD73low adult thymic c1 and c2 clusters in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice that was coupled with an increased frequency of the CD24posCD73+/- c0 cluster (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: There was an increased frequency of the CD24posCD73+/- c0 cluster in B6.Sh2d1a-/- adult thymus.
claims.source: For example, we observed a small but significant decrease in the frequency of the CD24highCD73low adult thymic c1 and c2 clusters in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice that was coupled with an increased frequency of the CD24posCD73+/- c0 cluster (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: SAP regulates the γδ T cell thymic developmental checkpoint at all ages.
claims.source: Like the SAP-dependent E17 c2 and D9 c1 clusters, the adult thymus c1 and c2 clusters were enriched in γδT17-associated Blk, Etv5, Sox13, Maf, and Rorc (mostly in c2) indicating that SAP regulates this γδ T cell thymic developmental checkpoint at all ages.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the gene expression and cluster frequency data across different ages.

claims.claim: There was a near complete loss of mature γδNKT cells in B6.Sh2d1a-/- adult thymus.
claims.source: Just as we observed in neonatal thymic γδ T cells, we noted a near complete loss of mature γδNKT cells (Zbtb16, Icos, and Il4-enriched γδT2 c8 cells and Tbx21, Slamf7, and Il2rb-enriched γδT1 c11 cells) as well as a decreased frequency of mature non-γδNKT γδT1 c10 cluster cells in B6.Sh2d1a-/- adult thymus (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: There was a decreased frequency of mature non-γδNKT γδT1 c10 cluster cells in B6.Sh2d1a-/- adult thymus.
claims.source: Just as we observed in neonatal thymic γδ T cells, we noted a near complete loss of mature γδNKT cells (Zbtb16, Icos, and Il4-enriched γδT2 c8 cells and Tbx21, Slamf7, and Il2rb-enriched γδT1 c11 cells) as well as a decreased frequency of mature non-γδNKT γδT1 c10 cluster cells in B6.Sh2d1a-/- adult thymus (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: The frequency of γδ T cells with an αβ T cell-like signature in the adult thymic γδ T cell dataset was minimal.
claims.source: Unlike the E17 and neonatal thymic datasets, however, the frequency of γδ T cells with an αβ T cell-like signature in the adult thymic γδ T cell dataset was minimal.
claims.evidence: This is a description of the adult thymus dataset.

claims.claim: There are multiple SAP-dependent developmental changes during neonatal and adult γδ T cell development.
claims.source: Collectively, these data supported the presence of multiple SAP-dependent developmental changes during neonatal and adult γδ T cell development—a reduction in the CD24posCD73neg SLAMF1+SLAMF6+ cluster enriched in γδT17 development-associated transcripts, an increased frequency of immature S1pr1-enriched γδ T cells, and decreased frequencies of both γδNKT cells (γδT1 and γδT2) and non-γδNKT γδT1 cells.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the findings from neonatal and adult thymus data.

claims.claim: A comparison of the frequencies of the top 100 neonate γδ TCR clonotypes between B6 and B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice revealed significant changes in the overall frequency of several TRGV1 and TRGV4 clonotypes.
claims.source: A comparison of the frequencies of the top 100 neonate γδ TCR clonotypes between B6 and B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice revealed significant changes in the overall frequency of several TRGV1 and TRGV4 clonotypes (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TCR clonotype frequency comparison shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: There was a profound loss of TRGV1 clonotypes utilizing the canonical TRAV15N-1 and TRAV15-1/TRDV6-1 γδNKT cell TCRs in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice.
claims.source: Consistent with a SAP-dependent loss of γδNKT, we observed a profound loss of TRGV1 clonotypes utilizing the canonical TRAV15N-1 and TRAV15-1/TRDV6-1 γδNKT cell TCRs (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TCR clonotype analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Loss of canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes was directly tied to the significant decrease of the γδT1 c8 and γδT2 c13 clusters.
claims.source: Loss of these clonotypes was directly tied to the significant decrease of the γδT1 c8 and γδT2 c13 clusters, in which nearly all these clonotypes resided.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the TCR clonotype and cluster frequency data.

claims.claim: Within the B6 γδT2 c13 cluster the vast majority (~86%) of TCR sequences were highly restricted canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes.
claims.source: Within the B6 γδT2 c13 cluster the vast majority (~86%) of TCR sequences were highly restricted canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes (Supplementary file 2) and nearly all of these clonotypes were also present in the γδT1 c8 cluster, consistent with the ability of γδNKT cells to produce both IFN-γ and IL-4.
claims.evidence: This is supported by TCR sequence analysis shown in Supplementary file 2.

claims.claim: Nearly all canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes in the c13 cluster were also present in the γδT1 c8 cluster.
claims.source: Within the B6 γδT2 c13 cluster the vast majority (~86%) of TCR sequences were highly restricted canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes (Supplementary file 2) and nearly all of these clonotypes were also present in the γδT1 c8 cluster, consistent with the ability of γδNKT cells to produce both IFN-γ and IL-4.
claims.evidence: This is supported by TCR sequence analysis shown in Supplementary file 2.

claims.claim: The B6 γδT1 c8 cluster contained a large proportion of canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes (~46% of c8 TCRs).
claims.source: In contrast, while the B6 γδT1 c8 cluster contained a large proportion of canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes (~46% of c8 TCRs), it also contained TCRs with a diverse pool of clonotypes that utilized TRGV1 (~70% of c8 TCRs), TRGV4, TRGV5, TRGV6, and TRGV7 that were present only in the c8 γδT1 cluster.
claims.evidence: This is supported by TCR sequence analysis.

claims.claim: The B6 γδT1 c8 cluster also contained TCRs with a diverse pool of clonotypes that utilized TRGV1 (~70% of c8 TCRs), TRGV4, TRGV5, TRGV6, and TRGV7 that were present only in the c8 γδT1 cluster.
claims.source: In contrast, while the B6 γδT1 c8 cluster contained a large proportion of canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes (~46% of c8 TCRs), it also contained TCRs with a diverse pool of clonotypes that utilized TRGV1 (~70% of c8 TCRs), TRGV4, TRGV5, TRGV6, and TRGV7 that were present only in the c8 γδT1 cluster.
claims.evidence: This is supported by TCR sequence analysis.

claims.claim: In neonates, the thymic γδT1 population is a mixture of γδNKT and 'non-γδNKT' γδT1 clonotypes, and each of these clonotype pools is SAP-dependent.
claims.source: Therefore, in neonates, the thymic γδT1 population is a mixture of γδNKT and 'non-γδNKT' γδT1 clonotypes, and each of these clonotype pools is SAP-dependent.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the TCR sequence analysis.

claims.claim: A closer examination of the neonatal thymic TRGV4 clonotypes revealed a significant decrease in the frequencies of γδT17-associated clonotypes with a germline-encoded TRDV5.
claims.source: Interestingly, a closer examination of the neonatal thymic TRGV4 clonotypes revealed a significant decrease in the frequencies of γδT17-associated clonotypes with a germline-encoded TRDV5 (Kashani, 2015; Figure 5B), some of which were identical to those that were redistributed to the αβ T cell-like c6 cluster in E17 γδ T cells (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TCR clonotype analysis shown in Figure 5B and a citation.

claims.claim: When TRGV4/TRDV5 clonotypes were mapped to their D9 clusters, there was a significant decrease in the frequency of TRGV4/TRDV5 clonotypes in the mature γδT17 c6 cluster.
claims.source: When these clonotypes were mapped to their D9 clusters, we noted a significant decrease in the frequency of TRGV4/TRDV5 clonotypes in the mature γδT17 c6 cluster (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TCR clonotype mapping shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: The immature E17 γδ TCR clonotypes that were redirected to the αβ T cell pathway in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice were underrepresented among the mature B6.Sh2d1a-/- neonatal γδ T cells.
claims.source: Taken together, these data indicated that the immature E17 γδ TCR clonotypes that were redirected to the αβ T cell pathway in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice were underrepresented among the mature B6.Sh2d1a-/- neonatal γδ T cells.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the TCR clonotype data across E17 and D9 timepoints.

claims.claim: SAP-deficiency results in a significant impairment in γδ T cell function in the periphery.
claims.source: We previously demonstrated that SAP-deficiency results in a significant impairment in γδ T cell function in the periphery (Dienz et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a previous finding by the authors.

claims.claim: γδ T cell IL-17 production is impaired in the lungs of young B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice, but this had largely corrected itself as the mouse reached maturity.
claims.source: Specifically, we observed that γδ T cell IL-17 production is impaired in the lungs of young mice, but that this had largely corrected itself as the mouse reached maturity.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a previous finding by the authors.

claims.claim: Both Vγ1 and Vγ4 IFN-γ production were significantly impaired in B6.Sh2d1a-/- adult lung and spleen.
claims.source: In contrast, we observed that both Vγ1 and Vγ4 IFN-γ production were significantly impaired in B6.Sh2d1a-/- adult lung and spleen.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a previous finding by the authors.

claims.claim: The initial annotation of the B6 lung γδ T cell transcriptome revealed the presence of 11 clusters.
claims.source: Our initial annotation of the B6 lung γδ T cell transcriptome revealed the presence of 11 clusters of the lung γδ T cells that we annotated based on cluster-specific gene expression and TRGV and TRDV usage (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This is a description of the lung γδ T cell dataset.

claims.claim: Based on their expression of signature cytokines and transcription factors, 2 γδT17 clusters (c1 and c4), 4 γδT1 clusters (c2, c3, c7, and c9), 1 γδTNKT-like cluster (c10), and a Cd24-enriched cluster (c5) were identified.
claims.source: Based on their expression of signature cytokines and transcription factors, we identified 2 γδT17 clusters (c1 and c4), 4 γδT1 clusters (c2, c3, c7, and c9), 1 γδTNKT-like cluster (c10) with very few cells, as well as a Cd24-enriched cluster (c5) (Figure 6B, C, Supplementary file 5).
claims.evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in figures and supplementary files.

claims.claim: The c1 and c4 γδT17 clusters were enriched in Slamf1.
claims.source: Consistent with previous observations, we noted that the c1 and c4 γδT17 clusters were enriched in Slamf1 and that the c2/c3/c7/c9 γδT1 clusters were enriched in Slamf7 and Slamf6 (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: The c2/c3/c7/c9 γδT1 clusters were enriched in Slamf7 and Slamf6.
claims.source: Consistent with previous observations, we noted that the c1 and c4 γδT17 clusters were enriched in Slamf1 and that the c2/c3/c7/c9 γδT1 clusters were enriched in Slamf7 and Slamf6 (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: Flow cytometric analysis revealed that SLAMF7 expression was restricted to the innate-like lung CD44+CD45RB+γδT1 cell population.
claims.source: Indeed, flow cytometric analysis revealed that SLAMF7 expression was restricted to the innate-like lung CD44+CD45RB+γδT1 cell population, and that γδT1 cells are SLAMF1-F6+F7+, while the CD44+CD45RB- γδT17 subsets are SLAMF1+F6-F7- (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: γδT1 cells are SLAMF1-F6+F7+, while the CD44+CD45RB- γδT17 subsets are SLAMF1+F6-F7-.
claims.source: Indeed, flow cytometric analysis revealed that SLAMF7 expression was restricted to the innate-like lung CD44+CD45RB+γδT1 cell population, and that γδT1 cells are SLAMF1-F6+F7+, while the CD44+CD45RB- γδT17 subsets are SLAMF1+F6-F7- (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: The c1 cluster corresponded to Vγ4 γδT17 (primarily TRGV4/TRDV5 and TRGV4/TRDV2-2).
claims.source: Further annotation using V(D)J profiling revealed that the c1 cluster corresponded to Vγ4 γδT17 (primarily TRGV4/TRDV5 and TRGV4/TRDV2-2) while the c4 cluster corresponded to lung Vγ6 (TRGV6/TRDV4) (Figure 6E, Supplementary file 6).
claims.evidence: This is supported by V(D)J profiling shown in Figure 6E and Supplementary file 6.

claims.claim: The c4 cluster corresponded to lung Vγ6 (TRGV6/TRDV4).
claims.source: Further annotation using V(D)J profiling revealed that the c1 cluster corresponded to Vγ4 γδT17 (primarily TRGV4/TRDV5 and TRGV4/TRDV2-2) while the c4 cluster corresponded to lung Vγ6 (TRGV6/TRDV4) (Figure 6E, Supplementary file 6).
claims.evidence: This is supported by V(D)J profiling shown in Figure 6E and Supplementary file 6.

claims.claim: The c10 cluster was enriched in Zbtb16, Il4, and Icos.
claims.source: The c10 cluster was enriched in Zbtb16, Il4, and Icos (Figure 6B, C) as well as TRGV1/TRAV15N-1 and TRGV1/TRDV6 sequences (Figure 6E, Supplementary file 6) consistent with γδNKT cells.
claims.evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figures 6B and 6C.

claims.claim: The c10 cluster was consistent with γδNKT cells.
claims.source: The c10 cluster was enriched in Zbtb16, Il4, and Icos (Figure 6B, C) as well as TRGV1/TRAV15N-1 and TRGV1/TRDV6 sequences (Figure 6E, Supplementary file 6) consistent with γδNKT cells.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from gene expression and TCR sequence data.

claims.claim: The TRAV15N-1 and TRDV6 sequences in the c10 cluster were, for the most part, non-canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes.
claims.source: We did note, however, that the TRAV15N-1 and TRDV6 sequences in the c10 cluster were, for the most part, non-canonical γδNKT cell clonotypes, suggesting a degree of flexibility in the TRAV15N-1 and TRDV6 CDR3 sequences that can be utilized by γδNKT cells.
claims.evidence: This is based on analysis of TCR sequences in the c10 cluster.

claims.claim: Vγ4 γδT1 cells exhibited a striking preference in the usage of TRAV13-4(DV7).
claims.source: Interestingly, while the γδT1 c2/c3/c7/c9 clusters contained primarily Vγ1 and Vγ4 T cells as expected, we noted that Vγ4 γδT1 cells exhibited a striking preference in the usage of TRAV13-4(DV7), and that TRGV4/TRDV7 pairings accounted for 80% of all Vγ4 clonotypes in the γδT1 clusters (Figure 6E, Supplementary file 6).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TCR sequence analysis shown in Figure 6E and Supplementary file 6.

claims.claim: TRGV4/TRDV7 pairings accounted for 80% of all Vγ4 clonotypes in the γδT1 clusters.
claims.source: Interestingly, while the γδT1 c2/c3/c7/c9 clusters contained primarily Vγ1 and Vγ4 T cells as expected, we noted that Vγ4 γδT1 cells exhibited a striking preference in the usage of TRAV13-4(DV7), and that TRGV4/TRDV7 pairings accounted for 80% of all Vγ4 clonotypes in the γδT1 clusters (Figure 6E, Supplementary file 6).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TCR sequence analysis shown in Figure 6E and Supplementary file 6.

claims.claim: Analysis of the γδT1 TRAV13-4/DV7 CDR3 sequences revealed a high level of diversity that showed no evidence of clonal expansions.
claims.source: Analysis of the γδT1 TRAV13-4/DV7 CDR3 sequences revealed a high level of diversity that showed no evidence of clonal expansions (Figure 6F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by CDR3 sequence analysis shown in Figure 6F.

claims.claim: Vγ1 γδT1 cells exhibited a more mild pairing preference where 44% of the γδT1 clonotypes utilized TRAV15N-1, TRAV15-1/DV6-1, or TRAV15D-2/DV6D-2 and 13% utilized TRAV13-4/DV7.
claims.source: Vγ1 γδT1 cells, in contrast, exhibited a more mild pairing preference where 44% of the γδT1 clonotypes utilized TRAV15N-1, TRAV15-1/DV6-1, or TRAV15D-2/DV6D-2 and 13% utilized TRAV13-4/DV7 (Supplementary file 6).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TCR clonotype analysis shown in Supplementary file 6.

claims.claim: These data formed a comprehensive map of B6 lung γδ T cell transcriptomes and revealed that lung innate-like γδT1, like γδT17 and γδNKT, are all characterized by preferential TCR γ- and δ-chain pairings.
claims.source: Together these data formed a comprehensive map of B6 lung γδ T cell transcriptomes and revealed that lung innate-like γδT1, like γδT17 and γδNKT, are all characterized by preferential TCR γ- and δ-chain pairings.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the lung γδ T cell data.

claims.claim: Vγ4 γδT1 exhibited a distinct preference for the utilization of TRAV13-4(DV7) chains with diverse CDR3.
claims.source: This was especially notable for Vγ4 and our data suggested that Vγ4 γδT1 exhibited a distinct preference for the utilization of TRAV13-4(DV7) chains with diverse CDR3.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the Vγ4 γδT1 TCR data.

claims.claim: Lung γδ T cell IFN-γ production is deficient in Sh2d1a-deficient mice.
claims.source: Consistent with our previous observation that lung γδ T cell IFN-γ production is deficient in Sh2d1a-deficient mice (Dienz et al., 2020), we observed a decrease in the frequency of the γδT1 c2, c3, and c7 clusters (Figure 7B).
claims.evidence: This is stated as a previous finding by the authors and is consistent with the current data.

claims.claim: There was a decrease in the frequency of the γδT1 c2, c3, and c7 clusters in B6.Sh2d1a-/- lung.
claims.source: Consistent with our previous observation that lung γδ T cell IFN-γ production is deficient in Sh2d1a-deficient mice (Dienz et al., 2020), we observed a decrease in the frequency of the γδT1 c2, c3, and c7 clusters (Figure 7B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: There was a striking decrease in the frequency of TRGV4/TRDV7-expressing cells in the lungs of B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice.
claims.source: Moreover, we observed a striking decrease in the frequency of TRGV4/TRDV7-expressing cells in the lungs of B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice (Figure 7C, D, Supplementary file 6), and we noted that we found no evidence of a compensatory increase in the frequency of other TRDV-expressing lung Vγ4 γδT1 cells in the B6.Sh2d1a-/- lung.
claims.evidence: This is supported by TCR expression analysis shown in Figures 7C and 7D and Supplementary file 6.

claims.claim: There was no evidence of a compensatory increase in the frequency of other TRDV-expressing lung Vγ4 γδT1 cells in the B6.Sh2d1a-/- lung.
claims.source: Moreover, we observed a striking decrease in the frequency of TRGV4/TRDV7-expressing cells in the lungs of B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice (Figure 7C, D, Supplementary file 6), and we noted that we found no evidence of a compensatory increase in the frequency of other TRDV-expressing lung Vγ4 γδT1 cells in the B6.Sh2d1a-/- lung.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a finding from the TCR expression analysis.

claims.claim: The SAP-dependent decrease in TRAV13-4/TRDV7 was independently confirmed in both lung and spleen using qPCR.
claims.source: We independently confirmed this SAP-dependent decrease in TRAV13-4/TRDV7 in both lung and spleen using qPCR (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and we demonstrated a significant decrease in the number of CD44+SLAMF7+ Vγ4 T cells in both the lungs and spleen of B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice (Figure 7E, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: There was a significant decrease in the number of CD44+SLAMF7+ Vγ4 T cells in both the lungs and spleen of B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice.
claims.source: We independently confirmed this SAP-dependent decrease in TRAV13-4/TRDV7 in both lung and spleen using qPCR (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and we demonstrated a significant decrease in the number of CD44+SLAMF7+ Vγ4 T cells in both the lungs and spleen of B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice (Figure 7E, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7E and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The decreased lung γδT1 did not appear to be due to an SAP-dependent decrease in homeostatic proliferation, nor to increased apoptosis.
claims.source: The decreased lung γδT1 did not appear to be due to an SAP-dependent decrease in homeostatic proliferation, nor to increased apoptosis, since we observed no significant change in lung γδ T cell BrdU incorporation or Annexin V staining in B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by BrdU incorporation and Annexin V staining data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: There was a loss of the c10 γδT2 cluster in B6.Sh2d1a-/- lung.
claims.source: In addition to the decrease in lung γδT1, we also noted a loss of the c10 γδT2 cluster consistent with the enrichment in SAP-dependent γδNKT TCRs in this cluster, and we observed an increased frequency of the Vγ4 γδT17 c1 cluster (Figure 7B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: There was an increased frequency of the Vγ4 γδT17 c1 cluster in B6.Sh2d1a-/- lung.
claims.source: In addition to the decrease in lung γδT1, we also noted a loss of the c10 γδT2 cluster consistent with the enrichment in SAP-dependent γδNKT TCRs in this cluster, and we observed an increased frequency of the Vγ4 γδT17 c1 cluster (Figure 7B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cluster frequency comparison shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: A comparison of the lung Vγ4 c1 γδT17 CDR3 sequences between B6 and B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice revealed significant alterations in the γδT17 c1 cluster TCR repertoire.
claims.source: Indeed, a comparison of the lung Vγ4 c1 γδT17 CDR3 sequences between B6 and B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice revealed significant alterations in the γδT17 c1 cluster TCR repertoire.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a finding from CDR3 sequence comparison.

claims.claim: There was a decreased frequency of TRGV4 chains that exhibited a germline-encoded CDR3γ (CSYGYSS) in B6.Sh2d1a-/- lung Vγ4 c1 γδT17.

results.result: SAP deficiency results in a significant loss of an immature Gzma+Blk+Etv5+Tox2+ γδT17 precursor population (c2 cluster) in E17 thymus, characterized by decreased expression of γδT17-associated genes including Blk, Etv5, Sox13, Maf, and Ccr2.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C65-C71, C75, C87-C89, and C91 collectively demonstrate through single-cell RNA-seq cluster frequency analysis, differential gene expression analysis, and flow cytometry that SAP deficiency leads to decreased frequencies of the c2 cluster and reduced expression of key γδT17 developmental genes. The data are internally consistent across multiple analytical approaches and include appropriate biological replicates.

results.result: SAP deficiency results in a significant increase in Cd4+Cd8+Rorc+Ptcra+Rag1+ thymic γδ T cells (c6 cluster) that exhibit characteristics of cells developing along the αβ T cell pathway.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C66, C74, C93-C94, and C97 demonstrate through cluster frequency analysis and flow cytometry that SAP deficiency increases the frequency of the c6 cluster expressing αβ T cell lineage markers. The phenotypic characterization is consistent across single-cell RNA-seq and flow cytometry validation.

results.result: SAP regulates TCR clonotype distribution during early γδ T cell development, promoting entry into the γδT17 pathway at the c5/c7 to c2 transition while inhibiting diversion into the αβ T cell-like c6 cluster, resulting in redistribution of specific clonotypes such as TRGV4/TRDV5 from the c2 to c6 cluster.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C85 demonstrate through TCR clonotype distribution analysis that SAP deficiency causes specific redistribution of TRGV4/TRDV5 clonotypes from the γδT17 c2 cluster to the αβ-like c6 cluster. The data show statistically significant changes in clonotype frequencies across clusters with appropriate biological replicates.

results.result: SAP-dependent diversion of E17 thymic γδ T cell clonotypes into the αβ T cell pathway is associated with decreased frequency of these mature clonotypes in neonatal thymus.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C134-C136, and C179 demonstrate through longitudinal TCR clonotype tracking from E17 to D9 that clonotypes diverted to the αβ pathway at E17 are underrepresented in mature neonatal γδ T cells. The analysis appropriately tracks specific clonotypes across developmental timepoints.

results.result: TRGV4/TRAV13-4(DV7)-expressing T cells represent a novel, SAP-dependent Vγ4 γδT1 subset that preferentially utilizes TRDV7 chains with diverse CDR3 sequences and accounts for 80% of Vγ4 clonotypes in lung γδT1 clusters.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C151-C153, C156, C159-C162, C171, and C181 demonstrate through V(D)J profiling, CDR3 sequence analysis, qPCR, and flow cytometry that Vγ4 γδT1 cells exhibit a striking preference for TRAV13-4(DV7) usage with diverse CDR3 sequences, and that this population is SAP-dependent. The finding is validated across multiple independent methods.

results.result: SAP deficiency results in near complete loss of mature γδNKT cells (both γδT1 and γδT2 subsets) characterized by loss of canonical TRAV15N-1 and TRAV15-1/TRDV6-1 TCR sequences in neonatal and adult thymus.
results.evaluation: Claims C115-C117, C122-C123, and C127-C133 demonstrate through cluster frequency analysis and TCR repertoire analysis that SAP deficiency causes profound loss of γδNKT cells expressing canonical TCR sequences. The data show consistent loss across developmental timepoints with appropriate characterization of TCR sequences.

results.result: SAP deficiency is associated with an altered γδT17 TCR repertoire in the periphery, characterized by decreased frequency of germline-encoded TRGV4 CDR3γ sequences and increased frequency of sequences with N/P additions.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C166-C170, C173, and C180 demonstrate through CDR3 sequence analysis that SAP deficiency alters the peripheral γδT17 TCR repertoire composition. The analysis shows statistically significant shifts in CDR3 sequence characteristics, though the functional significance of these changes is not fully established.

results.result: SAP-dependent γδ/αβ T cell lineage commitment regulates γδ T cell developmental programming and shapes the γδ TCR repertoire by simultaneously promoting progression through the γδT17 developmental pathway while inhibiting diversion into the αβ T cell pathway.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C177-C178, and C182 represent the overarching model supported by the collective data showing SAP's dual role in promoting γδT17 development and preventing αβ lineage diversion. This model is well-supported by the convergent evidence from cluster analysis, gene expression, TCR repertoire, and flow cytometry data.

results.result: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis of E17 thymic γδ T cells identifies 11 distinct clusters representing different developmental stages, including mature γδT17 (c8), mature γδT1 (c0/c9), immature γδT1 (c3), emigrating thymic cells (c4), immature γδT17 precursors (c1, c2, c7, c5), and αβ T cell-like cells (c6), with a developmental trajectory of c5→c7→c2→c10/c1→c8 for γδT17 cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C32-C64 collectively describe the comprehensive characterization of E17 thymic γδ T cell populations through integrated analysis of gene expression, surface protein markers, and TCR sequences. The cluster annotations are well-supported by multiple lines of evidence including marker gene expression, TCR repertoire analysis, and trajectory inference, with appropriate validation by flow cytometry.

results.result: SAP-dependent developmental checkpoints identified in E17 thymus are recapitulated in neonatal and adult thymus, with decreased frequencies of immature γδT17 precursor clusters and increased frequencies of S1pr1-enriched clusters in SAP-deficient mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C108-C114, C119-C121, and C125 demonstrate through cluster frequency analysis across multiple developmental timepoints that SAP regulates similar developmental checkpoints throughout thymic development. The consistency across ages strengthens the conclusions, though the magnitude of effects varies with age.

results.result: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis of adult lung γδ T cells identifies 11 clusters including 2 γδT17 clusters (c1: Vγ4, c4: Vγ6), 4 γδT1 clusters (c2, c3, c7, c9), and 1 γδNKT-like cluster (c10), with distinct SLAM family receptor expression patterns (γδT17: SLAMF1+, γδT1: SLAMF6+SLAMF7+).
results.evaluation: Claims C140-C150, C154-C155 provide comprehensive characterization of lung γδ T cell populations through integrated analysis of gene expression, surface markers, and TCR sequences. The cluster annotations are well-supported by V(D)J profiling and validated by flow cytometry showing SLAMF7 restriction to CD44+CD45RB+ γδT1 cells.

results.result: SAP deficiency in adult lung results in decreased frequencies of γδT1 clusters (c2, c3, c7), loss of the γδT2 c10 cluster, and increased frequency of the Vγ4 γδT17 c1 cluster, with the decreased γδT1 being due to specific loss of innate-like subsets rather than dysregulated cytokine production.
results.evaluation: Claims C158, C164-C165, and C172 demonstrate through cluster frequency analysis and functional characterization that SAP deficiency causes specific alterations in lung γδ T cell subset composition. The conclusion that decreased IFN-γ production is due to loss of specific subsets rather than functional impairment is well-supported by the data.

results.result: The decreased lung γδT1 in SAP-deficient mice is not due to altered homeostatic proliferation or increased apoptosis.
results.evaluation: Claim C163 is supported by BrdU incorporation and Annexin V staining data showing no significant differences between B6 and B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice. This negative result appropriately rules out these mechanisms, though additional mechanisms were not fully explored.

results.result: Blk expression is uniquely dependent on SAP, while Lck and Fyn expression are not appreciably altered in SAP-deficient immature E17 γδ T cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C73 demonstrate through pseudobulk analysis that Blk shows SAP-dependent expression while other Src family kinases do not. However, the authors note that Lck differential expression was close to the threshold, suggesting some caution in interpretation. The specificity for Blk is reasonably well-supported.

results.result: SAP deficiency does not affect the overall number of E17 γδ T cells or overall PLZF expression levels in E17 thymic γδ T cells, despite affecting specific developmental subsets.
results.evaluation: Claims C86, C90, and C92 report negative findings that help define the specificity of SAP's effects. These are appropriately supported by flow cytometry data and help establish that SAP's effects are on developmental programming rather than overall γδ T cell generation.

results.result: The E17 thymic γδ T cell dataset comprises 5278 cells from B6 (n=2597) and B6.Sh2d1a-/- (n=2681) mice.
results.evaluation: Claim C31 describes the dataset composition, which is a straightforward methodological detail that is verifiable from the data. The sample sizes are adequate for single-cell analysis.

results.result: Comparison of E17 γδ TCR clonotypes between B6 and B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice reveals no significant changes in overall clonotype frequency, but closer examination reveals significant changes in the distribution of specific TCR clonotypes.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C77 appropriately distinguish between overall repertoire diversity and specific clonotype distribution changes. This finding is important for understanding that SAP affects clonotype fate rather than overall TCR diversity.

results.result: There is a significant increase in TRGV4/TRDV7 clonotypes in the Il2ra+ c5 cluster in SAP-deficient mice.
results.evaluation: Claim C80 is supported by TCR clonotype distribution analysis. However, the biological significance of this specific increase is not fully explored in the context of the other findings.

results.result: There is a striking decrease in Zbtb16 expression among all immature neonatal γδ T cells compared to E17.
results.evaluation: Claim C100 describes a developmental change in PLZF expression between E17 and neonatal stages, which is supported by gene expression data and consistent with previous reports. This is a descriptive finding about normal development.

results.result: Neonatal thymic γδNKT cells are characterized by enrichment of canonical TRGV1/TRAV15N-1 or TRAV15-1/DV6-1 sequences, with γδT2 cells expressing Zbtb16, Icos, and Slamf6, while γδT1 cells express Tbx21, Klrb1c (NK1.1), and Slamf7.
results.evaluation: Claims C103-C107 provide detailed characterization of neonatal γδNKT cell subsets through TCR repertoire analysis, differential gene expression, and flow cytometry validation. The characterization is thorough and internally consistent.

results.result: Comparison of the top 100 neonatal γδ TCR clonotypes between B6 and B6.Sh2d1a-/- mice reveals significant changes in the overall frequency of several TRGV1 and TRGV4 clonotypes.
results.evaluation: Claim C126 is supported by TCR clonotype frequency analysis. This finding sets up the more detailed analyses of specific clonotype changes that follow.

results.result: SLAM/SAP signaling pathway regulates the development of multiple innate-like T cell lineages including NKT, γδNKT, γδT1, γδT17, and MAIT cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C23-C27 summarize prior work from the literature establishing the broad role of SLAM/SAP signaling in innate-like T cell development. These are appropriately cited background claims that provide context for the current study.

results.result: Background knowledge about γδ T cell biology, including their classification into functional subsets, tissue distribution, roles in immunity, TCR signal strength models, SLAM family receptor structure and function, and developmental timing.
results.evaluation: Claims C8-C22, C28-C30 represent established background knowledge appropriately cited from the literature. These provide necessary context for interpreting the current findings.

results.result: Background information about neonatal thymic development, dataset characteristics, and previous findings on SAP-deficient γδ T cell function in the periphery.
results.evaluation: Claims C98-C99, C118, C124, C137-C139 provide background context and describe dataset characteristics. These are appropriately supported by citations to prior work or are straightforward descriptions of the data.

results.result: SAP plays a critical role in the development of IFN-γ and IL-4-producing γδNKT cells as well as γδT1 and γδT17, but the timing and mechanism of SAP function during γδ T cell development is unknown.
results.evaluation: Claims C175-C176 summarize prior knowledge and identify the knowledge gap that motivates the current study. These are appropriately cited and accurately represent the state of the field.

results.result: SLAM/SAP signaling plays a role in shaping the γδ TCR repertoire.
results.evaluation: Claim C174 is a conclusion drawn from the collective TCR repertoire data showing altered clonotype distributions in SAP-deficient mice. This is well-supported by the data, though the precise mechanisms remain to be fully elucidated.

results.result: SAP deficiency results in a significant loss of an immature Gzma+Blk+Etv5+Tox2+ γδT17 precursor population (c2 cluster in E17, c1 cluster in neonates). This was observed across E17, neonatal, and adult thymus, with decreased frequencies of these clusters and reduced BLK expression levels in SAP-deficient mice.
results.evaluation: All three reviewers affirm the study's findings without questioning these specific results. Reviewer 1 states 'the conclusions of the study are supported by well thought-out experiments and compelling data,' and Reviewer 3 notes the study is 'very thorough, thoughtfully interpreted' with no challenges to these developmental checkpoint findings.

results.result: SAP deficiency resulted in a significant increase in Cd4+Cd8+Rorc+Ptcra+Rag1+ thymic γδ T cells (c6 cluster in E17, c14 cluster in neonates), representing γδ T cells diverted into the αβ T cell developmental pathway. These cells exhibited an immature phenotype lacking canonical γδT17-associated markers.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding as a key contribution. Reviewer 3 specifically highlights 'a particularly interesting element is the role of SLAM-SAP in preventing gd17 progenitors from switching fates and adopting the ab fate,' indicating explicit support for this result.

results.result: SAP-dependent diversion of E17 thymic γδ T cell clonotypes (particularly TRGV4/TRDV5 and TRGV1/TRDV4) into the αβ T cell developmental pathway was associated with decreased frequency of these mature clonotypes in neonatal thymus and an altered γδ TCR repertoire in the periphery.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the TCR repertoire findings. The editor's summary states the study 'uncovers the complex role of the SLAM-SAP pathway in developing specific gamma-delta T cell subsets' and notes the evidence is 'compelling, backed by high-quality data,' implicitly supporting these repertoire observations.

results.result: TRGV4/TRAV13-4(DV7)-expressing T cells (Vγ4/Vδ7) are identified as a novel, SAP-dependent Vγ4 γδT1 subset. These cells showed striking preference for TRAV13-4(DV7) usage (80% of Vγ4 clonotypes in γδT1 clusters) with diverse CDR3 sequences, and their frequency was markedly decreased in SAP-deficient lung and spleen.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly accept this novel finding. Reviewer 1's summary states 'the authors define TRGV4/TRAV13-4(DV7)-expressing T cells as a novel, SAP-dependent Vγ4 γδT1 subset' without critique, and all reviewers note the study's contributions to understanding γδ T cell subsets without questioning this discovery.

results.result: There was a striking loss of γδNKT cells (both IL-4-producing γδT2 c13 cluster and IFN-γ-producing γδT1 c8 cluster) in SAP-deficient neonatal and adult thymus, with profound loss of canonical TRAV15N-1 and TRAV15-1/TRDV6-1 γδNKT cell TCRs.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question these findings on γδNKT cells. Reviewer 1 notes the study 'reveals the role of SAP-dependent events in generation of γδ TCR repertoire' and Reviewer 3 states the study 'adds significantly to our understanding of the contribution of the SLAM-SAP pathway to lineage specification,' supporting these observations.

results.result: SAP-dependent γδ/αβ T cell lineage commitment regulates γδ T cell developmental programming. SAP operates at an early stage during or after IL2ra downregulation, positively regulating entry into the γδT17 pathway at the c5/c7 to c2 transition while simultaneously inhibiting diversion into the CD4+CD8+ αβ T cell-like pathway.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept this mechanistic model. Reviewer 3 explicitly notes 'a particularly interesting element is the role of SLAM-SAP in preventing gd17 progenitors from switching fates and adopting the ab fate,' directly supporting the dual regulatory function proposed by the authors.

results.result: The adult lung γδT17 TCR repertoire is altered in SAP-deficient mice, with decreased frequency of germline-encoded TRGV4 CDR3γ sequences and increased frequency of sequences with N/P additions, associated with shifts in TRDV2-2 usage and altered clonotype frequencies. This suggests SLAM/SAP signaling shapes the γδ TCR repertoire.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these peripheral repertoire findings. The editor notes the study 'highlights the importance of SLAM-SAP signaling in determining innate gamma-delta T cell sublineages and their T cell receptor repertoires,' explicitly supporting these conclusions about repertoire shaping.

results.result: Neither Lck nor Fyn expression was appreciably altered in SAP-deficient immature E17 γδ T cells, suggesting that Blk expression was uniquely dependent on SAP among Src family kinases.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 specifically asks 'In the subsets of the γδ T cells that exhibit reduced BLK expression in B6. SAP KO mice, have the authors examined the expression of Lck and/or Fyn?' The authors addressed this in revision, and Reviewer 1 states 'The author has adequately addressed all the reviewers' comments,' indicating acceptance of this finding.

results.result: Mature γδT17 clusters (c8 in E17, c1 and c4 in lung) were enriched in IL-17-associated transcripts and SLAMF1, while mature γδT1 clusters were enriched in IFN-γ-associated transcripts, SLAMF7, and SLAMF6. Flow cytometry confirmed SLAMF7 expression was restricted to CD44+CD45RB+ γδT1 cells.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question these characterization findings. The editor's summary notes the evidence is 'compelling, backed by high-quality data obtained through advanced single cell proteogenomics techniques,' supporting the validity of these cluster annotations and marker identifications.

results.result: The c1 and c2 clusters in E17 thymus represent immature γδT17 precursors enriched in developmental genes (Blk, Maf, Sox13, Etv5, Rorc). The c2 cluster (Gzma+) shows Rorclow expression and enrichment in TRGV4 with restricted TRDV usage, while c1 shows higher Rorc expression. BLK expression precedes RORγt during development, supporting a c5→c7→c2→c1→c8 developmental trajectory.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these developmental trajectory findings without critique. Reviewer 3 notes the study is 'very thorough, thoughtfully interpreted' and 'adds significantly to our understanding,' implicitly supporting these detailed developmental characterizations.

results.result: The c6 cluster in E17 thymus represents γδ T cells developing along an alternative αβ T cell pathway, characterized by enrichment in Cd8a, Cd8b1, Cd4, Rag1, Rag2, Ptcra, and Rorc expression without canonical γδT17 markers (Maf, Blk, Ccr2). These cells exhibited CD4CD8 DP phenotype with immature characteristics.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge this characterization. Reviewer 3 specifically highlights this as 'a particularly interesting element,' indicating explicit acceptance of the identification and characterization of this alternative developmental pathway.

results.result: Pseudobulk analysis of immature E17 clusters revealed 234 differentially expressed genes between B6 and SAP-deficient mice (148 decreased, 86 increased). Downregulated genes reflected γδT17-associated genes in c2/c1 clusters, while upregulated genes were enriched in the c6 cluster, identifying these as SAP-dependent developmental checkpoints.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these differential expression findings. Reviewer 1 states 'the conclusions of the study are supported by well thought-out experiments and compelling data,' and no reviewer questions the pseudobulk analysis or its interpretation.

results.result: The neonatal thymus contains a CD24neg73posSLAMF1negSLAMF6high γδT2 cluster (c13) enriched in Il4, Il13, Zbtb16, Cd40lg representing IL-4-producing γδNKT cells with canonical TRGV1/TRAV15N-1 sequences. These cells co-express SLAMF6 and ICOS, while γδT1 cells express NK1.1, Tbx21, and SLAMF7.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these neonatal γδNKT characterizations. The overall acceptance of the study's findings on γδNKT cells and the lack of specific critique of these markers indicates implicit support for these observations.

results.result: In lung, the c1 cluster corresponds to Vγ4 γδT17 (TRGV4/TRDV5 and TRGV4/TRDV2-2), c4 to Vγ6 (TRGV6/TRDV4), and c10 to γδNKT cells enriched in Zbtb16, Il4, Icos with TRGV1/TRAV15N-1 sequences. The c10 TRAV15N-1 sequences were mostly non-canonical, suggesting CDR3 flexibility.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these lung γδ T cell characterizations. The editor's summary notes the study provides 'a comprehensive map of B6 lung γδ T cell transcriptomes,' and no reviewer questions these cluster annotations or TCR usage patterns.

results.result: SAP deficiency did not affect overall E17 γδ T cell numbers but resulted in reduced BLK expression levels in immature γδT17 cells. Interestingly, SAP did not affect overall PLZF expression levels in E17 thymic γδ T cells despite PLZF induction often being associated with SLAM/SAP signaling.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question these findings on protein expression levels. The observation about PLZF is presented as an interesting exception, and reviewers' overall acceptance of the data quality supports these observations.

results.result: In neonatal and adult thymus, there was increased frequency of immature S1pr1-enriched clusters and small but significant decreases in SAP-dependent immature clusters enriched in γδT17-associated genes (Blk, Etv5, Sox13, Maf, Rorc), indicating SAP regulates this developmental checkpoint at all ages.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these findings across developmental stages. Reviewer 1 notes the study 'furthers our understanding of the importance and complexity of the SLAM-SAP signaling pathway,' supporting the conclusion that SAP functions consistently across ages.

results.result: Lung γδ T cell IFN-γ production is deficient in SAP-deficient mice due to decreased frequency of γδT1 clusters (c2, c3, c7), not due to dysregulated cytokine production or altered homeostatic proliferation/apoptosis, but rather due to specific loss of innate-like γδT1 subsets.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept this mechanistic interpretation. Reviewer 1 notes the study 'reveals the role of SAP-dependent events' in γδ T cell function, and no reviewer questions the conclusion that the functional defect results from cell loss rather than dysregulation.

results.result: The E17 thymus dataset (5278 cells total) contained multiple clusters including c3 (immature γδT1 with invariant TRGV5/TRDV4), c4 (emigrating Ccr9+S1pr1+ γδ T cells), and c5/c7 (recently developed from DN2/DN3 with Il2ra, cell cycle genes), representing early developmental stages.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question these cluster identifications or dataset characteristics. The editor notes the evidence is 'backed by high-quality data obtained through advanced single cell proteogenomics techniques,' supporting the validity of these annotations.

results.result: The Vγ1 repertoire in E17 thymus was dominated by TRGV1/TRDV4 clonotypes (35% of all TRGV1), with two semi-invariant clonotypes comprising 17.4%. These were located in immature γδT17 clusters and represented dominant IL-17-producing Vγ1 clonotypes, verified by flow cytometry. The Il4-enriched c2 cluster did not contain canonical γδNKT sequences.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these E17 repertoire findings without critique. The detailed TCR analysis is part of the comprehensive characterization that reviewers praise, with no specific concerns raised about these observations.

results.result: Overall γδ TCR clonotype frequency was unchanged between E17 B6 and SAP-deficient mice, but closer examination revealed significant changes in distribution of specific clonotypes, including increased TRGV4/TRDV7 in the Il2ra+ c5 cluster in SAP-deficient mice.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these nuanced repertoire findings. The observation that overall frequency is unchanged while specific distributions shift is consistent with the reviewers' acceptance of the study's detailed analytical approach.

results.result: Neonatal and adult thymus showed striking decrease in Zbtb16 expression among immature cells, decreased frequency of mature γδT17 and γδNKT clusters, and decreased frequency of non-γδNKT γδT1 cells in SAP-deficient mice. Adult thymus had minimal γδ T cells with αβ T cell-like signature unlike E17/neonatal datasets.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these developmental stage comparisons. The comprehensive analysis across multiple timepoints is part of what Reviewer 3 describes as 'very thorough,' and no concerns are raised about these observations.

results.result: Among top 100 neonatal γδ TCR clonotypes, there were significant frequency changes in TRGV1 and TRGV4 clonotypes. The neonatal thymic γδT1 population is a mixture of γδNKT (~46% of c8 TCRs with canonical sequences) and diverse non-γδNKT γδT1 clonotypes (utilizing TRGV1, 4, 5, 6, 7), with both pools being SAP-dependent.

results.result: Vγ1 γδT1 cells exhibited milder TCR pairing preference than Vγ4, with 44% utilizing TRAV15N-1/TRAV15-1/DV6-1/TRAV15D-2/DV6D-2 and 13% utilizing TRAV13-4/DV7.
